Honour
ON-'r
n. and v. (rendering Hebrew kābōd, kābad, and Greek timē, doxa)
From Old French onor, from Latin honor, esteem or public office; the Authorized Version's spelling with -our is retained here as the dictionary's standard. The Hebrew kābad means literally to be heavy, and its noun kābōd is weight — so that to honour someone is to treat him as weighty, and glory is heaviness. The Greek timē comes from the vocabulary of price and valuation: to honour is to reckon at a high value.

Biblical Definition

Honour in Scripture is the giving of due weight, and the direction of it is what makes it either obedience or idolatry. It is owed first to God: “Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase” (Pro 3:9) — honour rendered not in sentiment but in the first and best of what one has, which is why the firstfruits and not the leftovers are named. It is owed to the Son equally with the Father, and the Lord makes this a test: “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him” (Joh 5:23) — which forecloses every religion that professes to revere God while denying Christ. It is owed to parents by the fifth commandment, the first with promise: “Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land” (Exo 20:12), and the Lord rebuked the Corban tradition that let a man evade the support of his parents under a show of piety. It is owed within the church to those who labour in it: “Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine” (1Ti 5:17), where the following verse about the ox and the labourer's hire shews that material support is included. And it is owed broadly — honour all men; honour the king; in honour preferring one another.

Webster 1828 Definition

The giving of due weight and value; owed to God in the firstfruits of one's substance, to the Son equally with the Father, to parents under the fifth commandment, to faithful elders in double measure, and in its measure to all men and to lawful authority.

expand to see more

HONOUR, n. 1. The esteem due or paid to worth; high estimation; respect; veneration.

2. That which is due or paid in token of esteem; reverence; dignity; as, honour thy father and thy mother.

3. Reputation; good name; a nice sense of what is right, and of what is due to others.

4. The Hebrew word signifies weight; to honour is to account weighty, and glory is heaviness. The Greek word is from the vocabulary of price, to value highly.

5. HONOUR, v.t. To revere; to respect; to treat with deference and submission, and perform relative duties to. Honour the LORD with thy substance. Prov. 3.

Key Scripture

Exodus 20:12 — "Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee."

Proverbs 3:9 — "Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:"

John 5:23 — "That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him."

1 Timothy 5:17 — "Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine."

Modern Corruption

Honour has been redefined as a feeling owed only where it is felt to be deserved, so that the commanded honour of parents, elders, and magistrates is made conditional on their merit — and, in the other direction, honour is claimed by office-holders as immunity from correction.

expand to see more

Scripture attaches honour to relation and office, not to performance. The fifth commandment carries no clause exempting children of poor parents, and Peter told slaves to be subject not only to the good and gentle but also to the froward. This does not make honour unlimited: the same Scripture requires that we obey God rather than men, forbids following a father into idolatry, and provides for the rebuke and even the removal of an elder. But the modern instinct — that respect must be earned before it is given, and withdrawn the moment it is disappointed — is not the biblical one. Honour is first a duty rendered to God through the station He has appointed, and only secondarily a response to the character of the person occupying it. That is why it can be commanded at all.

The corresponding abuse belongs to those in office who invoke honour to escape accountability. Paul's instruction about elders is the pattern of the balance: double honour in one verse, and in the same passage the rule that an accusation against an elder shall be received before two or three witnesses, and that those who sin are to be rebuked before all, that others also may fear. Honour and correction are not alternatives. The Lord Himself honoured His mother from the cross and yet withstood Peter to his face; He rebuked the Pharisees for using Corban to strip the fifth commandment of its cost. Honour that never costs the giver anything is flattery, and honour that never permits correction is tyranny.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kābad is to be heavy, and so to honour; its noun kābōd is weight and hence glory. Greek timē is price or value, giving timaō, to value highly; doxa is glory or reputation.

expand to see more

Hebrew kābad (H3513) — to be heavy, to be honoured, to glorify; the same verb used of Pharaoh hardening (making heavy) his heart.

Hebrew kābōd (H3519) — weight, glory, honour; the word behind the glory that filled the tabernacle and the weight of glory in 2Co 4:17.

Hebrew hādar (H1921) — to honour, to adorn, to shew respect; used in Lev 19:32, thou shalt honour the face of the old man.

Greek timē (G5092) — a valuing, price, honour; used of double honour for elders (1Ti 5:17) and of the price paid for the field of blood.

Greek timaō (G5091) — to value, to honour; the verb of the fifth commandment as quoted in the Gospels and of honouring the Son (Joh 5:23).

Usage

"Of honour toward God: honour the LORD with thy substance (Pro 3:9); them that honour me I will honour (1Sa 2:30)."

"Of honour toward Christ: that all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father (Joh 5:23)."

"Of honour in family, church, and commonwealth: honour thy father and thy mother (Exo 20:12); double honour for elders (1Ti 5:17); honour all men, honour the king (1Pe 2:17)."
